page.head.meta_content_1: Compare 9 crypto cards for Ukraine using real purchases. Crypto payments, fees, cashback and UAH exchange costs, with rankings, first-hand experience and evidence.
page.head.title_1: Crypto cards in Ukraine — 9-card comparison and ranking
page.hero.p_1: Within a few minutes, I made nine identical UAH 158 purchases at one physical shop, one with each crypto card. I compared actual debits, fees and cashback to help choose a crypto card for payments in Ukraine and international subscriptions.

page.methodology.intro: 9 October 2026 · 9 identical purchases of UAH 158 at one store within a few minutes.
page.methodology.debit: Debit: before balance minus after balance. Exceptions are USDT spent on the completed OKX screen, Bybit’s USDT debit in asset history, Trustee’s exact receipt and Solid’s Available to spend. Initial balances are kept separate from completed payments.
page.methodology.benchmark: The NBU rate on the test date was 44.8526 ₴/$, giving a $3.522649746… purchase equivalent. Deviation includes visible costs, not only FX spread. I do not add included fees twice.
page.methodology.included: I deduct displayed Solid $0.11 and COCA $0.03 before credit, Bybit’s 36 credited points at 0.002 USDT/point = 0.072 USDT under redemption terms, and Kolo / WhiteBIT BTC at a fixed valuation. Bybit point redemption into USDT is unverified. Trustee Points contribute $0 to the current cash calculation.
page.methodology.model: Potential assumes $1,000 of eligible purchases over a full month on the base or next tier, after the monthly cap and annual fee / 12. WhiteBIT uses the upper bound for selected categories; extra category bonuses from other programs are excluded from the ranking. FX fees, funding, balance income and token capital cost are assessed separately. COCA limits how much cashback can be claimed, rather than how much accrues. This is a terms-based model, not measured monthly profit.
page.methodology.btc: I value displayed Kolo BTC and credited WhiteBIT BTC at a fixed $82976.035/BTC quote. This is neither spendable USD nor a measured sale rate; each card’s details contain the valuation and source.
page.methodology.precision: One small purchase and rounded balances limit ranking precision. Sub-cent differences may depend on rounding; fixed fees change results at larger amounts. An app status does not always prove card-network settlement.
page.sources.issuer_note: I used my confirmations, BIN lookups and public terms. OKX’s BIN databases conflict, so Bano remains provisional. WhiteBIT’s help page names JSC Hash Bank, while BIN lookups show Insbank; the reason is unresolved. A BIN database does not replace the individual card agreement.

earning.title: Earning
earning.method_title: How I calculate Earning and total benefit
earning.method: With even spending, average balance = ($1,000 + $0) / 2 = $500. APR: $500 × rate × 30 / 365. For APY, I use the equivalent daily rate: $500 × 30 × ((1 + APY)^(1/365) − 1). The model does not reinvest income. If the source does not specify APR/APY, I show both estimates as a range of assumptions, not a guaranteed payout.
earning.assumptions: I assume a constant rate and eligibility of the entire average balance. Subscriptions paid early, deposits in installments, and time outside an eligible balance change the result. Estimates exclude taxes and unknown claim costs; each card lists its program’s limits.
earning.combined: I calculate total benefit as cashback + spendable income − FX, conversion, funding and tier fees. I subtract each tier fee once. Balance income is not attributed to the UAH 158 purchase and does not change its ranking. In this model, 5% a year covers only about 0.20% of the monthly budget; debit cost and cashback remain the main factors for UAH spending.
earning.cards.bybit.note: USDT Auto-Earn is enabled; Auto Deduction during payment is verified by the 3.6407 USDT redemption from Savings. This funded the purchase; it was not income. I use the USDT rate rather than the “up to 10.89%” banner; rate tiers and caps for larger balances are unconfirmed.

earning.cards.simple.note: Income accrues automatically on the card balance; claims start at 1 USDC. The rate is variable; caps and tiers for larger balances are unknown. I have not tested a payout; the screen does not establish whether this rate requires a referral code.

cards.okx.experience: I would choose it primarily for the UAH purchase exchange rate: the controlled test had the lowest debit before cashback. USDG is unavailable in my Ukrainian scenario, so cashback and balance rewards do not work for me. If cashback were available, I would consider OKX the best option for individual use. Viewing full card details requires 2FA each time, and that can be inconvenient. Cashback and yield on certain currencies in the exchange account are positives. Online acceptance is uneven: RozetkaPay declined my payment in the test.

cards.coca.experience: Convenient overall. There is a USD account funded with USDT or USDC, and a EUR account funded with EURC. Supported networks depend on the token. Withdrawals are fast, but only USDC or EURC via Base is available. There is cashback and yield on the USD account balance.

cards.keyone.experience: Fund with USDT or USDC, but a top-up fee applies. There is no cashback; crypto withdrawals use Base. I have not found anything particularly special about this card.
cards.kolo.funding: Funding Arbitrum → Wallet: 10 → 10 USDT. Arbitrum withdrawal including an existing balance: 11.46 − 1 fee → 10.46 USDT received.
cards.kolo.experience: I would also choose it for regular use, especially with family. Share Card is straightforward: everyone the card is shared with can approve payments. Cashback and several funding and withdrawal options are available. Kolo also offers a USD card, but issuance is unavailable for Ukraine as of November 9, 2026. I therefore use the EUR card here; I have not separately tested EUR purchases.
cards.simple.funding: Polygon funding: 10 USDT → displayed 9.98 USDC; exact credit unknown. Withdrawal via the Simple wallet → my Base wallet: 9.989909 USDC received, with no token deduction on either leg.
cards.simple.experience: Everything is simple. Almost. There are a few extra steps, but overall it is very convenient to use. It is a shame there is no cashback.
cards.solid.funding: Funding Arbitrum → Fuse: 10 → 9.997 USDT; direct Fuse: 10 → 10 USDT. Withdrawal via Fuse: all 19.997 USDT received; Solid paid the fee. For withdrawing this amount via Arbitrum, the app showed a 0.33 USDT fee; I did not choose that option.

USD and EUR are available, with several funding and withdrawal routes. During earlier checks, payment approval required opening Approvals in the card settings.

page.faq.3.question: How can I get a crypto card in Ukraine?
page.faq.3.answer: Choose a card and check availability for your country of residence and the service requirements. Visit the official website, register and complete the required identity verification. Check issuance and ongoing fees before applying. Each card has a non-referral button, and invitation links are labelled separately.
page.faq.4.question: How do crypto payments work in shops and online?
page.faq.4.answer: To the merchant, paying with crypto through a crypto card is an ordinary card payment in fiat currency. Fund the required balance using a supported asset and network, then transfer from the wallet to the card if needed. Pay as with a regular payment card: the service uses the crypto balance or previously exchanged funds. Each card’s full cycle and details show the specific route and debits.
page.faq.5.question: Which crypto cards support Apple Pay and Google Pay?
page.faq.5.answer: All nine cards in this research support adding the card and paying with Apple Pay and Google Pay. These are Bybit, COCA, KeyOne, Kolo, OKX, Simple, Solid, Trustee Plus and WhiteBIT. Add the card from the service app or through Wallet, enter the card details if needed and complete issuer verification.
page.faq.6.question: Can I spend USDT or USDC with a crypto card?
page.faq.6.answer: Yes, the research includes purchases funded with USDT and USDC. The card settlement currency can still be USD or EUR. Supporting a token for deposits does not guarantee that the same token is debited directly for purchases. Exchange rates and fees affect the final amount, so the tests compare the asset actually spent.
page.faq.7.question: How do I fund a crypto card and withdraw the remaining balance?
page.faq.7.answer: Open the money-flow diagram on the chosen card page. It separates funding, the payment balance and withdrawals. Before sending funds, match the asset, network, minimum amount and fee against the current in-app terms. Some cards require an internal wallet or exchange transfer. Route costs are shown separately from purchase costs.

A new rank requires a comparable test.

pages.simple_gasless_scope: Gasless applies to sending from the self-custody wallet. On the listed routes, network fees are paid in the token sent; there is also paid activation once per network. Both amounts are shown before confirmation. Card top-ups and swaps have separate fees.

pages.simple_gasless_exclusions: Polygon supports native USDC, not USDC.e. USDT on Arbitrum, USDC on Optimism, Avalanche, TRON, TON, Bitcoin and other tokens still require native gas. This is not the full withdrawal-network list. Migration and one-time activation do not affect the Manual actions criterion, which counts internal transfers before card payments.
pages.whitebit_fee_scope: The fee help article and product FAQ agree. The effective date is unknown, so this clarifies current terms rather than proving an increase on a particular date. Check applicable final fees in the card interface.
flow.simple_gasless_activation: New engine: paid Gasless activation once on Base; the amount is shown before confirmation.
flow.simple_gasless_fee: Network fee in USDC. Current amount unknown; the old zero-deduction test is not a new-engine tariff.

cards.solid.faq.0.question: Is Solid Card suitable for everyday payments in Ukraine?
cards.solid.faq.0.answer: Solid Card is my current choice for regular use in Ukraine: it has USD and EUR, cashback, and several funding and withdrawal routes. In October 2026, I made 91 merchant payments totalling $1,403.09. This reflects a month of my use, rather than just one controlled payment.
cards.solid.faq.1.question: Solid Core cashback: how much did I receive in a month of use?
cards.solid.faq.1.answer: Yes, my October cashback came to $30. Solid does not include cashback in the statement, so I show this amount separately from purchase debits. The $30 does not establish a guaranteed rate for the next month: the result depends on eligible payments and the Rewards terms.
cards.solid.faq.2.question: Can I pay for ChatGPT with crypto through Solid Card?
cards.solid.faq.2.answer: Yes, the historical tests include a $100 USD ChatGPT payment with $3 displayed cashback under Standard 3%. I have not separately reconciled cashback payout for this particular payment or its full crypto debit. During earlier checks, approving an online purchase required opening Approvals in the card settings, which I find an extra step.
cards.solid.faq.3.question: What are the fees for withdrawing USDT and USDC from Solid?
cards.solid.faq.3.answer: My completed USDT withdrawal test on Fuse had no additional token deduction. For USDC on Fuse, the app also showed no minimum or fee. Other networks showed variable Stargate Bridge and LayerZero charges, so I do not apply the Fuse conditions to every route.
cards.kolo.faq.0.question: Can I use Kolo Card as a family crypto card?
cards.kolo.faq.0.answer: Share Card lets me give other family members shared access to the card. Everyone I share it with can approve payments. In my experience, this is a convenient and straightforward way to use one card for shared family purchases.
cards.kolo.faq.1.question: Is the Kolo USD card available in Ukraine?
cards.kolo.faq.1.answer: Kolo offers a USD card, but issuance is unavailable for Ukraine as of November 9, 2026. I therefore use the EUR card in this research and in the Ukrainian scoring scenario. The existence of a USD program does not mean I can use it in Ukraine.
cards.kolo.faq.2.question: What cashback does Kolo Card offer: 1% or 2%, and what are the caps?
cards.kolo.faq.2.answer: For the EUR card, the introductory 2% lasts only for the first 30 days; the regular rate is then 1%. Cashback is in BTC, with regular-rate caps of €1 per purchase and €100 per month. Large purchases reduce the effective percentage, and received BTC is not a spendable USD balance.
cards.kolo.faq.3.question: Kolo USDC withdrawals: which networks, fee and minimum apply?
cards.kolo.faq.3.answer: In my recorded terms, the fee is 1 USDC and the transfer minimum depends on the network: 5 USDC on Ethereum, or 1 USDC on BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum and Base. The fee is added to the transfer amount. Polygon withdrawals are absent from the list I checked.
cards.trustee_plus.faq.0.question: Trustee Plus: what is my review of the card and its drawbacks?
cards.trustee_plus.faq.0.answer: In my test, Trustee Plus gave me the worst experience among these cards: a separate wallet-to-card transfer, minimum amounts, extra fees and waiting. I found the process slow and insufficiently clear. After this test, I cannot recommend it for everyday payments.
cards.trustee_plus.faq.1.question: How do I fund the Trustee Plus card with USDT or USDC?
cards.trustee_plus.faq.1.answer: In my completed test, I first funded the card separately from the internal wallet. The card top-up minimum was 10 plus a fee. Public documentation also describes Auto Top-Up, but I have not tested that automatic route and keep it separate from my completed test.
cards.trustee_plus.faq.2.question: What are the withdrawal fee and minimum in Trustee Plus?
cards.trustee_plus.faq.2.answer: On the routes I checked, the external transfer minimum was 10, with a fee on top; the lowest displayed fee was 0.50. A balance equal to the minimum could therefore be insufficient. I also swapped USDC to USDT and added funds to prepare the withdrawal; completed receipt in the external wallet remains unconfirmed.
cards.trustee_plus.faq.3.question: Does Trustee Plus offer cashback, and what do Trustee Points provide?
cards.trustee_plus.faq.3.answer: In my records, Trustee Points are internal points for a seasonal prize competition. I have not established a fixed payout in cash or stablecoins. I therefore do not deduct them from purchase costs in the monetary comparison.
cards.okx.faq.0.question: What exchange rate does OKX Card give for UAH payments in Ukraine?
cards.okx.faq.0.answer: When the exchange rate for a UAH purchase is the main priority. In the identical 158 UAH test, OKX had the lowest debit before cashback. This is the result of one controlled payment, rather than a guarantee of the best rate for every amount or date.
cards.okx.faq.1.question: Does OKX Card USDG cashback work in Ukraine?
cards.okx.faq.1.answer: USDG is unavailable in my Ukrainian scenario, so its linked cashback and balance yield do not work for me. I do not apply other regions’ terms to my card. In my comparison, the main OKX advantage is therefore the measured cost of the UAH payment.
cards.okx.faq.2.question: Does an OKX Card online payment work through RozetkaPay?
cards.okx.faq.2.answer: RozetkaPay declined OKX Card in my test. I keep this as a practical limitation, but it does not establish rejection by every merchant or permanent incompatibility with the service. For an important purchase, I would keep a backup payment method.
cards.okx.faq.3.question: Funding and withdrawing USDT in OKX Pay: is there an X Layer fee?
cards.okx.faq.3.answer: In my X Layer test, the full 10 USDT was credited and returned to the external wallet without a USDT deduction. I account for the initial sender gas separately. This is the tested X Layer route; Ethereum showed separate swap and transfer costs.
cards.bybit.faq.0.question: Bybit Card in Ukraine: how is the Funding balance used for payments?
cards.bybit.faq.0.answer: In my scenario, the card uses the shared Funding balance, so I do not need a separate manual card-account top-up before paying. I found deposits and withdrawals convenient. The card is also part of the exchange account, which matters when choosing the service.
cards.bybit.faq.1.question: What is Bybit Card cashback: Base and Beta caps and point redemption?
cards.bybit.faq.1.answer: Bybit cashback has monthly caps and is awarded in points. In the recorded general schedule, Base is capped at 5 USDT, while Beta has separate requirements. The AU program differs, so the active terms must match the specific card; I also distinguish credited points from their redemption.
cards.bybit.faq.2.question: Does Bybit Card work with Apple Pay and Google Pay?
cards.bybit.faq.2.answer: Yes, Bybit Card supports adding the card and paying through Apple Pay and Google Pay. The inconvenience I encountered concerns a different process: viewing my full card details requires 2FA each time. This adds a step when entering details manually online, rather than requiring 2FA for every phone payment.
cards.bybit.faq.3.question: Does RozetkaPay accept Bybit Card payments?
cards.bybit.faq.3.answer: RozetkaPay declined Bybit Card in my test. I therefore do not equate a convenient exchange balance and cashback with guaranteed acceptance by every merchant. This is an observed case from my use, rather than a test of every online service.
cards.coca.faq.0.question: COCA Card in Ukraine: which USD and EUR accounts are available?
cards.coca.faq.0.answer: COCA has a dollar account funded with USDT or USDC and a euro account funded with EURC. This provides a choice of currency for different expenses. Deposit networks depend on the token; the deposit list does not mean the same routes are available for withdrawals.
cards.coca.faq.1.question: What cashback does COCA Card offer, and when can I claim it?
cards.coca.faq.1.answer: In the recorded terms, COCA Starter accrues 1% cashback with a monthly claim cap of $15. Standard offers 3% with a $25 claim cap and requires staking 300 COCA. After a 14-day wait, rewards must be claimed manually, from $1 and at most once per 24 hours. Other bonuses, including subscription rebates, may use the same allowance.
cards.coca.faq.2.question: Withdrawing USDC and EURC from COCA: which network and fee apply?
cards.coca.faq.2.answer: In the scenario I checked, withdrawals use USDC or EURC on Base. In my completed USDC test, the external wallet received exactly the internally credited amount without an additional USDC deduction. This is not a promise of free withdrawals for any token on any network.
cards.coca.faq.3.question: COCA balance yield: does 5% APY apply to the entire balance?
cards.coca.faq.3.answer: No. My app snapshot shows 5% APY and claims from $1, but the documentation has conflicting wording about the eligible balance. Applying the rate to all $1,000 in the scoring model is marked as an assumption. It is a model, rather than measured annual earnings.
cards.keyone.faq.0.question: KeyOne Card: what are the USDT and USDC funding fees?
cards.keyone.faq.0.answer: Under the recorded Free terms, crypto funding costs 0.8% plus a network component. In my full test, 10 USDT resulted in 9.910683 USDC returned; this is the nominal difference for the entire route, rather than an isolated top-up fee. I account for external sender gas separately.
cards.keyone.faq.1.question: Is KeyOne Premium worthwhile, and does it offer purchase cashback?
cards.keyone.faq.1.answer: I found no numerical KeyOne cashback program in the terms I read. Premium costs €149 per year and reduces the crypto funding fee from 0.8% to 0.33%, plus network costs. I assess its benefit through savings on deposits, rather than purchase rewards. Whether Premium pays for itself depends on the volume of deposits.
cards.keyone.faq.2.question: Funding KeyOne through SEPA and ACH: what should I check?
cards.keyone.faq.2.answer: KeyOne’s public materials describe SEPA and ACH routes, so funding is not limited to crypto. I have not tested these routes in this research. I therefore make no finding about a specific route’s availability for my account, actual processing time or full funding cost.
cards.keyone.faq.3.question: What is the fee for withdrawing USDC from KeyOne on Base?
cards.keyone.faq.3.answer: My completed test delivered 9.910683 USDC to the external wallet on Base, matching the internal credit and withdrawal debit exactly. There was no additional USDC deduction at that step. This does not remove the funding cost or establish a free tariff for every future transfer.
cards.simple.faq.0.question: How do I fund Simple Card with crypto and withdraw the remaining balance?
cards.simple.faq.0.answer: The route I checked supports direct card funding, so a separate internal transfer before paying is unnecessary. Returning funds followed a different route: card → embedded wallet → external address. I distinguish the two processes so that withdrawal steps are not added to an ordinary purchase.
cards.simple.faq.1.question: Does Simple Card offer cashback if Auto Earning is available?
cards.simple.faq.1.answer: I have not established a permanent cashback program with defined rates and caps in the terms I read. I therefore add no Simple cashback to the purchase-cost calculation. Individual promotions and Auto Earning have different terms and do not replace regular purchase cashback.
cards.simple.faq.2.question: What are Simple Gasless fees for USDT and USDC transfers?
cards.simple.faq.2.answer: No. On supported routes in the new wallet, the network fee can be paid in a stablecoin instead of the native token. Each network requires a separate paid activation. I keep the older Base USDC test without deductions as historical evidence; I have not measured the new wallet’s current full fee.
cards.simple.faq.3.question: Simple Wallet: does the TON address change, and how can I recover access?
cards.simple.faq.3.answer: The Dynamic MPC migration documentation requires keeping the recovery code: recovery after losing access is impossible without it. The TON address for new deposits also changes. These are the documented migration terms; my completed old-wallet test does not verify the new process.
cards.whitebit.faq.0.question: WhiteBIT Nóva USD: what are the card payment fees?
cards.whitebit.faq.0.answer: The documents checked on November 9, 2026 state 1.5% + $0.20 per transaction, with a possible additional 1.5% conversion charge. The fixed $0.20 particularly affects small purchases. A dollar account alone therefore does not mean low-cost payments.
cards.whitebit.faq.1.question: What is WhiteBIT Nóva cashback: categories, 10% and the $25 cap?
cards.whitebit.faq.1.answer: No. In my account snapshot, higher rates depend on selected categories and the merchant’s MCC, with a shared monthly cap of $25. Categories must be selected before purchase. Rewards can be in BTC or WBT; their nominal valuation is not dollars already received.
cards.whitebit.faq.2.question: How do I fund WhiteBIT USD Card from the main exchange balance?
cards.whitebit.faq.2.answer: My checked scenario uses the exchange’s shared balance: after funding the main account, a separate manual card transfer was unnecessary. I find that convenient, but the card remains linked to the exchange account. I account for payment fees and withdrawal rules separately.
cards.whitebit.faq.3.question: What did a WhiteBIT Nóva USD payment in UAH cost in my test?
cards.whitebit.faq.3.answer: The controlled 158 UAH purchase on October 9, 2026 debited 3.82 USDT for a $3.57 card amount. This is already the measured total debit. The current tariff’s effective date is unknown, so adding its fees again could double-count costs; a current rank requires a new comparable test.
